name: Air duct and dryer vent cleaning

pf.license.need: Cleaning air ducts and dryer vents needs no state license in most places. Where a state or city licenses home improvement or HVAC work, its form asks for it. Cutting, sealing or repairing ducts, replacing a dryer vent, and gas or electric work can need an HVAC or contractor license, or a gas fitter's license, where the state requires one; this business cleans only. Asbestos removal and mold removal over the state's size cutoff are separate licensed trades and are not offered. The vent shop's counter: business registration only.
pf.license.ask: The company's business registration, or its contractor or HVAC license, where the state's form asks for one.
pf.license.who_holds: The business. Crew members and shop techs need no license of their own unless the state's form says so.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.insurance_bond: General liability and workers' comp are common. 'Insured' is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Crews work inside homes: the business's own word that they are checked, or a check Rosie holds where the state's rules require one. It is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.trade_certificates: A trade group's certificate for duct or dryer vent cleaning is not a state license. It shows in the business's own words, never as checked by Rosie.
pf.license.not_this_work: Asbestos removal, mold removal over the state's size cutoff, pest and animal removal, and furnace or dryer repair are licensed or separate trades. They aren't duct or vent cleaning.

pf.services.capacity: A whole-home duct cleaning takes a crew of two with a truck-mounted or portable vacuum. A dryer vent takes one technician. A shop drop-off needs one person at the counter.
pf.services.nobody_home: No. An adult must be home: vents are opened, the system is off during the work, and the customer signs off at the end. Roof-exit work is done from the roof or the ground with the adult home.
pf.services.online: No. A camera video of the ducts is sent after the visit, not a video visit.
pf.services.not_offered: Furnace, air conditioner and dryer repair, duct sealing or replacement, mold or asbestos removal, animal removal, chimney work.
pf.services.drop_off_slots: Filters, registers and vent covers are booked into drop-off slots by the shop's daily number, with no washer named; the items go to a shop tech with the skill once they're in.

before_times: What needs cleaning: the air ducts, the dryer vent, or both
Air ducts: how many heating and cooling systems, how many vents and returns, and about how many square feet
Dryer vent: electric or gas dryer, how long the run is, how many floors, and whether it exits through the wall or the roof
When the ducts or the dryer vent were last cleaned
Signs of trouble: clothes taking two cycles to dry, a very hot laundry room, lint outside, dust blowing from the vents
A home built before 1980, or ducts wrapped in old insulation (an asbestos check comes first)
Any animals heard in the ducts or the vent
At the counter: which items, and what they're made of
after_a_time: Who will be home: the customer, or someone else (their name and mobile go on the secure page)
Where the furnace or air handler is, and the attic or crawl space access
Where the dryer vent comes out, and parking
Own or rent: the landlord's OK for anything beyond cleaning
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult who owns or rents the home, or someone the owner allows. A renter books cleaning; the landlord's OK is needed for anything beyond cleaning.

words: smoke or flames from a dryer, a vent, a furnace or the ducts
a gas smell or a carbon monoxide alarm
suspected asbestos on ducts or pipes
a mold patch over the state's size cutoff
dead animals or heavy droppings in the ducts
an attic or crawl space floor that isn't safe
what_happens: Smoke or flames now: get everyone out of the house, then call 911 from outside. Rosie never places the call. No booking until the fire department clears it.
A gas smell or a carbon monoxide alarm: get everyone outside now, then call 911 and the gas company. No booking until it's safe.

Signs of a clogged dryer vent (clothes damp after a full cycle, a very hot dryer or laundry room, lint at the outside vent) are not an emergency: stop using the dryer until the vent is cleaned. The booking goes on.

Suspected asbestos, mold over the cutoff, droppings, sewage: Rosie says a duct cleaner can't take that part on and points to a specialist. The rest of the home can still be booked with that part left out.
Sparking wires or an unsafe attic floor: stay out of the area; no booking for it until it's fixed.
Animals heard in the ducts or the vent: a wildlife company first. Protected birds nesting in an outside vent stay until they leave; no cleaning or cap removal until then.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: Yes, with the part left out (asbestos, mold, droppings, sewage, wiring, a floor), and for signs of a clogged dryer vent. No, for smoke or flames now, a gas smell or a carbon monoxide alarm.

pf.first_steps.first_clean: Before the main visit: an asbestos check for ducts wrapped in old insulation in an older home; a free walkthrough for a multi-unit or whole-building job; photos first for a post-remodel cleaning.
pf.first_steps.wildlife: Live animals in the ducts or vent: a wildlife company first, licensed where the state requires one. The booking can move with no fee.
pf.first_steps.plan: A yearly dryer vent plan starts after the first visit. It has its own yes, apart from the booking, and the terms are texted back.
prep_for_reminder: Clear about 3 feet around the vents, the furnace and the dryer
Move small items and rugs off the floor vents
At the counter: bring the filters dry, with their frames
pf.first_steps.size_check: A heavy grease set at the counter: a short look first, so the price is set before any work (the example: a $25 look).

pf.visit.check_in: The check-in code at the door, entered by the crew lead. The on-my-way text names the crew lead, with a photo.
pf.visit.counter: At Lee Vent Shop: the code is given at the counter when the items are left. Status words IN, DRYING, READY. READY comes with a photo. Pick-up only by the customer or someone they name.
pf.visit.how_it_works: Vents are covered or opened, the system is turned off, and the ducts are cleaned with a brush and a vacuum under negative pressure. The dryer vent is cleaned from the dryer to the outside. Before and after photos, or a camera video of the ducts, are kept with the job.
pf.visit.weather: A roof exit is worked only when it's dry and not windy. Otherwise the vent is cleaned from inside and from the ground, and a roof check is booked again for free if needed.
pf.visit.findings: Nothing is sealed, repaired or replaced at a cleaning unless it's quoted and OK'd. A broken vent cover or a crushed vent hose is quoted with its lines before any work. Over the owner's limit (the example: $500), the owner OKs it first.
pf.visit.a_hazard_found: Suspected asbestos wrap, mold, droppings or a crushed gas line: that part stops at once, and a written note goes to the customer, kept with the photos.
pf.visit.work_sold_at_the_home: A right to cancel only where the state's rules give one.
pf.visit.proof_done: DONE with the bill's lines and the after photos or the camera video. The report goes with the receipt.

pf.money.start: At the customer's place: a card saved at booking for the late-cancel and nobody-home fee, and the saved card is charged when the crew texts DONE; or nothing taken and Rosie texts the bill. Counter drop-offs: nothing taken, paid at the counter at pick-up.
pf.money.deposits: None by default. Sam can set a deposit or the full price per service, within the state's caps (the example: a dryer vent cleaning paid in full when booking). Deposit cap: from the state form.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel and nobody home: the business's own fee (the example: $89), never more than what was paid now when money was paid now. Needs a saved card. The owner confirms each one; no answer, no fee. No card saved, no fee.
pf.money.plans: A yearly dryer vent plan: its own yes first, each visit booked and paid like a single one, a text each September to pick a time, and one tap ends it. Rosfield's $2 counts once for each booked visit.
pf.money.tax: No tax line unless the owner sets a rate where the state taxes the work.
pf.money.insurance_claims: A home insurance claim for duct or vent work is the customer's own; the customer gets the receipt and the photo report.

never_in_texts: Gate or lock codes, and where a key is kept
Photos from inside the home. The photo report and camera video open on the secure page.
Health reasons, like an allergy behind a product to avoid
pf.messages.danger_words: Smoke, flames, gas and carbon monoxide words always get the safety message first, before anything else.

pf.staff.crews: Two per whole-home duct job: a lead, who holds the entry code and texts DONE, and a helper. A person who works alone (a dryer vent technician) adds an emergency contact, and a missed safety check gives that contact the job's address only.
pf.staff.licenses: None per person unless the state's form says so. A trade group's certificate shows only as the person gave it, not checked.
pf.staff.new_person_ok: A crew member the customer hasn't booked is offered by text first, never sent without an OK.
pf.staff.who_oks: The owner OKs fees, walkthrough quotes, repairs over the limit and same-day jobs. The office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
pf.staff.stand_ins: Another crew lead with the same skill, at the same window and price.

plans: The plan's terms show before any card is asked: how often, the price a visit, when it's charged, that it runs until ended, and how to end it.
The plan gets its own yes, apart from the booking, and the terms are texted back.
A price change is told 30 days ahead, or more where the state's rules ask.
pf.rules.written_estimate: A written estimate before work above an amount: from the state form.
pf.rules.add_on_at_home: A right to cancel only where the state's rules give one for work sold at the home.
pf.rules.landlord: A renter books cleaning; the landlord's OK is needed for anything beyond cleaning.
pf.rules.protected_birds: Birds the law protects, nesting in an outside vent: no cleaning or cap removal until they've left.
pf.rules.live_animals: The business doesn't remove live animals. A wildlife company does it first, licensed where the state requires one.
pf.rules.warranty: The owner's own guarantee, shown on the receipt (the example: a missed vent is re-cleaned free within 30 days).
pf.rules.records: 7 years, with the before and after photos and the camera video.

matter_most: Smoke or flames at any point: get out and call 911 first; the owner is told
Signs of a clogged dryer vent: stop using the dryer until it's cleaned; the booking goes on
Suspected asbestos wrap, mold, droppings or sewage found: that part stops with a written note; the rest can go on
Animals or nesting birds in the ducts or vent: a wildlife company first; the visit can move with no fee
Wet or windy on a roof-exit day: worked from inside and the ground; a roof check booked again for free
An attic or crawl space that is blocked or unsafe: that part is skipped and noted, never forced
A missed vent: tell the business within 30 days; a free return visit (a redo, never money from Rosie)
Nobody home at the door: the no-show steps, with the owner's OK before any fee
A crew member is out: a new person is offered first; no answer, the visit moves with no fee
Items at the counter that nobody picks up: reminders; after the free days, a storage fee only if the owner starts it, after written notice
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
Pilot: chimney (from), refitted Oct 27. Duct and dryer vent cleaning runs like a set service at a home: a 2-hour arrival window, a crew lead who holds the entry code, an adult at home, findings quoted and OK'd, a yearly plan for the dryer vent, and a counter at the shop. The chimney's shape fits (per-flue pricing becomes per-system and per-run pricing); what it lacks is added: the asbestos check for old wrapped ducts, mold and droppings that are left out, animals and nesting birds in a vent, a roof exit worked only when dry, and before and after photos or a camera video.
Flow B is the usual side: Lee Duct Care (air duct cleaning, plus dryer vent cleaning as its second kind of work). Flow A is the less usual side: Lee Vent Shop, Sam's second company, where a customer drops off range hood filters, furnace filters, registers, vent covers and lint trap screens to be degreased and picks them up clean (the cleaner's drop-off, re-themed). Vent washing is done at the shop only: the both-places and other-place branches are off in both flows.
Money (B): main list|card|card (card saved for the $89 late-cancel and nobody-home fee, charged $179 when the crew texts DONE). Also list|none|bill (nothing taken, Rosie texts the bill), photos|deposit|card (post-remodel duct cleaning $640 from photos: $160 now, $480 at DONE), visit|card|card (whole-building cleaning priced at the walkthrough). The only deposit is on the post-remodel cleaning; list-price cleanings are paid on completion. Money (A): list|none|counter (main), list|card|counter, list|full|none, photos|none|counter, visit|none|counter. A fee is never more than what was paid now. An added service is paid at the visit. Nothing is charged without a yes; no hold.
The sign-up money card (S1-13) keeps the master's example reply (some services paid in full): the dryer vent cleaning is the one the example pays in full. It is an example, the owner decides.
Never sent now: duct and vent cleaning is booked ahead. S2-30 branch 1 is off and the booking choices are limited (B: a set time in a window; A: a set start); the rows and lines that said 'takes jobs sent now' (S2-30, S1-21) are re-worded.
Plan: a yearly dryer vent plan, $150 a visit, every 12 months, with its own yes (B5-20, B5-21: the master's own example is the same yearly plan); each September a text to pick an October time; one tap ends it. The first plan visit is a year after the first cleaning, so no plan date runs backward.
Danger: smoke or flames from a dryer, vent or furnace, a gas smell or a carbon monoxide alarm stop the booking (911, no booking). Signs of a clogged dryer vent (clothes damp after a full cycle, a very hot dryer, lint outside) are not an emergency: stop using the dryer, the booking goes on. Suspected asbestos wrap, mold over the cutoff, droppings and sewage: that part is left out and a specialist is named. The danger examples in B3-11 and B3-18 use the clogged-vent signs; B3-19 uses smoke; everyday examples use none of the stop words.
Own steps: B7-x01 (animals or nesting birds in the ducts or the vent: a wildlife company first, no fee to move).
No tips, stages, documents, waitlist or monthlybill facts. Facts: plans, firststeps, dropoff, photos, extrawork. Switches: none (cancelright off: add-ons are done at the visit). Settings: arrive A setstart / B window; cutoff A 24 hours before, B 24 hours before.
Licenses: duct and dryer vent cleaning need none in most places; the form asks where the state or city requires a registration or an HVAC or contractor license. Furnace and dryer repair, duct sealing, mold and asbestos removal and animal removal are not offered. A trade group's certificate shows only as checked.
Names: crew leads Marek and Nadia (flow B), shop techs Noor and Kofi (flow A). Addresses: 38 Alder Ct (the home), 22 Foundry St (the vent shop), 120 Quarry Rd (the travel area). Registration numbers use the REG-0612 format. The example times (8 to 10am windows) are the master's; Sam sets the real hours.
Kept words: 'leak' (the privacy leak in the shared rules), 'color' (race, color), 'visit fee' (the master's own words for a fee owed after a no to a price).
